question: Can a geometry-controlled minimum qualifying active observation plus frozen RoMa indoor dense cycle evidence provide exact same-door support and NONE assignment on fresh SceneNN targets?

predecessor.observed_failure: The maximum-baseline view policy left only two of four true diagonals supported by EfficientLoFTR; a separate one-pass consumed-cohort RoMa diagnostic showed strong symmetric cycle support on the one easiest true pair and essentially zero cycle support on ordinary cross-door pairs.
predecessor.structural_change: Replace adversarial maximum-baseline selection with the minimum qualifying 0.3 m active displacement before applying symmetric dense cycle evidence. No matcher threshold sweep is performed.

independent_motivation.source_inference: RoMa is a robust dense matcher with strong reported ScanNet indoor correspondence results. Dense symmetric warp certainty permits an explicit cycle-consistency support predicate instead of treating relative appearance rank as absolute identity evidence.

source_selector.inventory: Previously materialized SceneNN XML labels plus official HTTP HEAD metadata only; no selected PLY, trajectory, ONI, RGB-D, or model score opened before admission.
source_selector.target_label: normalized lowercase text must match door followed by zero or more digits
source_selector.candidate_rule: Among unconsumed candidates with at least one qualifying door and official ONI Content-Length, choose the four smallest ONI payloads, tie by scene ID; choose the lowest numeric qualifying door instance in each selected scene.

provider.name: SceneNN
provider.sensor: Asus Xtion PRO consumer RGB-D camera
provider.license_boundary: Educational and research use; raw SceneNN payloads remain local and are not redistributed.

pre_rgb_selector.pair_ranking: minimum qualifying camera-centre baseline, then maximum minimum visible target pixels, maximum minimum visibility ratio, earlier frames

renderer.near_plane_face_rule: reject unless every vertex is beyond near plane
renderer.visibility_rule: target depth finite and no farther than full-scene depth plus 0.005 m

pre_rgb_selector.failure_semantics: If any selected target lacks a qualifying pair, stop NOT_EVALUABLE without substituting a scene or changing geometry rules.

matcher.windows_runtime_reason: Official package disables local custom correlation on non-Linux and uses the standard correlation path.
matcher.input: expand the evaluator-visible target-mask tight box by 1.25, clamp and crop unmasked RGB
matcher.absolute_support: both directions must have at least one percent of the 864-square grid above official certainty and within six-pixel normalized symmetric cycle error, and a majority of each direction's high-certainty pixels must be cycle consistent
matcher.rank_score: geometric mean of the two directional cycle-consistent fractions
matcher.zero_assignment: strict reciprocal maximum among absolutely supported pairs; unsupported pairs are NONE
matcher.adaptation: none; CUDA inference; no fresh-result threshold or model fitting

baseline.descriptor: L2-normalized mean final patch tokens on the identical unmasked context crop
baseline.assignment: strict reciprocal cosine with no absolute support

forbidden_after_rgb_access: change scenes, targets, selected frames, action geometry, crop expansion, model, resolutions, certainty threshold, cycle tolerance, support fractions, score, reciprocity, scenarios, or decision gate
drop a target or failed scenario
fit a threshold or model on the fresh results
claim_boundary: A pass is fresh SceneNN Development evidence that a geometry-controlled active observation and truth-cropped RoMa dense cycle evidence can support same-door/NONE decisions. It remains same-provider, evaluator-mask-conditioned indoor RGB, not raw-phone detection, named entrance, portal ownership, access, traversability, waypoint, arrival, HANDOFF_READY, user benefit, deployment, or safety evidence.
